words: Human brain dependence does not exclude an unembodied God, because jubilation and sadness are mental rather than neural properties, leaving materialism to explain identity and agency.
critique: Strongest feature: It blocks the inference from human brain dependence to the impossibility of an unembodied divine mind, while jubilation and sadness distinguish mental predicates from physical descriptions. Principal limitation: Those examples illustrate conceptual differences but do not establish ontological irreducibility, and the passage compresses how self-identity, intentionality, and agency exclude reductive or epiphenomenal alternatives. Live burden: The pro side must justify the bridge from mental properties to an immaterial person, showing why competing material accounts cannot preserve identity and causal agency over time. Locked score: The exact score of 74 fits because responsiveness and relevance are stronger in directly contacting the brain-dependence objection, whereas evidence warrant and calibration are weaker because categorical conclusions outrun the brief examples and narrow engagement with alternatives.
